liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help on the Way** (3 reviews): Opening with Help, Slipknot and Franklin's Tower signaled a hot night ahead, according to the reviewer; The Help, Slip, Franklin's opening sequence is described as tight [11][18][21]
- **Eyes of the World** (2 reviews): Reviewer played this Eyes as a New Year's intro song at a party in Vermont; Eyes opening the second set is called sweet, and the reviewer felt transported [16][18]
- **So Many Roads** (1 review): Garcia had a music stand in front of him during this song, before lyric monitors [17]
- **U.S Blues** (1 review): U.S. Blues closed the show, accompanied by a wonderful light show [13]

## The recordings

- **gd92-03-05.sbd.lutton.5240.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 154 min; rated 4/5 by 22 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer ranks this soundboard among the best-sounding ones they have downloaded; Reviewer calls the download's sound top-notch, apart from a first few songs not quite mixed right; Reviewer finds the sound decent but says at least twenty other downloads are better [1][11][13][19]
- **gd1992-03-05.155826.FOB.SchoepsMasterDAT.Brotman.Metchick.Anon.Noel.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 18 songs; 161 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd92-03-05.sbd.hinko.27422.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 154 min; rated 3.29/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1992-03-05.176634.mtx.tobin.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 156 min [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended with two friends in a sold-out crowd that went wild at the opening Help on the Way [13]
- This was the reviewer's first Dead show, and hearing the recording brought back memories [14]
- Reviewer was arrested earlier that day, made bail, and stood near the front on a floor with no seats [17]
- Reviewer sees this as the end of the band's last high point with Hornsby [17]
- Reviewer bought tickets for both nights outside a dorm at the Mosque; this was their first show [18]
- Reviewer was present; says Hornsby was outrageous but Vince ruined a number of tunes [19]
- Reviewer found the two shows fun but solid and somewhat predictable, with no crazy surprises [20]
- From one row from the front, reviewer saw Garcia seeming unhappy, glaring at Phil and ignoring Bob [21]
- Reviewer says this show is not even close to being better than Cornell [19]
- Reviewer calls this the most unpleasant Dead concert they saw, despite great Warfield Theater experiences [21]
- Reviewer would point listeners to the Sunday Vegas show in May instead, as best of 1992 [22]
- Reviewer calls it a solid show, not worth mentioning in the same breath as Cornell [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd92-03-05.sbd.lutton.5240.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> DAT> ?> CD> EAC> SHN [1]. Also: Soundboard to DAT to unknown step to CD, then EAC and SHN by Ben Luton [1]
- **gd1992-03-05.155826.FOB.SchoepsMasterDAT.Brotman.Metchick.Anon.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Recording by Dave Brotman & Jeff Metchick; transferred by Transfer by Anonymous Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel January 08, 2022; source: Source: FOB Schoeps CMC3 MK4’s (ORTF) > Tao Research > M1000 cables > Panasonic SV-255mod (16/48) > Master DAT Location: 20th Row Center, Mics on Stand @ 7' [4]. Also: Tapes were adjusted in an SV3800, have no emphasis; Ted Mattes organized and Ron Keyser supplied the patch source [4]
- **gd92-03-05.sbd.hinko.27422.sbeok.flacf**: source: SBD > DAT > C > DAT > CD > EAC > FLAC [2]
- **gd1992-03-05.176634.mtx.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (48/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (48/16) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1992-03-05 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1992-03-05-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [24]
